description: Run the full deterministic L1 code-vetting pipeline over a target tree and return a bounded metrics summary plus a severity-ranked markdown report. Default (no 'target_path') is a self-vet of the platform's own git worktree, byte-compatible with the prior behavior. An optional ABSOLUTE 'target_path' vets a FOREIGN repo/source tree instead, READ-ONLY (the engine never writes into the target): validated fail-loud (absolute, exists, is a directory, must not resolve inside our own worktree), enumerated git-preferred (the target's own 'git ls-files') with a structural walk fallback for a non-git tree (curated excludes, NO gitignore emulation), with the derived target_class + enumeration mode + detected language stacks + file count recorded. Every foreign run also carries a bounded source_role_partition plus a technology_fingerprint nested in the existing target object. The fixed, exactly-reconciled fingerprint reads only enumerated well-known manifests/configs under size caps with strict duplicate-key-rejecting JSON; malformed, duplicate, oversize, symlink, and unsupported JSONC inputs become per-probe unreadable gaps. It keeps each package/Deno runtime scope distinct, separates direct declarations from co-scoped npm v2/v3 resolutions and lock-only evidence, inventories bounded Expo Router route paths without reading route content, records Supabase/Deno topology separately, and surfaces executable JS config as presence-only/unmodeled. Parsed role_overrides are the only source-role confirmation input: confirmed non-product facts remain visible but do not support product routing; unconfirmed stays unconfirmed. Its capability_needs use capability keys only and are deterministic routing evidence with execution_status 'not_run_by_fingerprint' — routing is not execution and no row claims clean/pass. The fingerprint executes no config, target code, network, subprocess, install, second crawl, sandbox, or symlink traversal and discloses the mutable-worktree/non-atomic boundary. Optional 'role_overrides' accepts at most 32 doctrine-backed, per-run literal path-prefix declarations ({path_prefix, role, doctrine_locator, declaring_session}); longest boundary-aware prefix wins. Only surface-quality dimensions are partitioned into product/non_product/unconfirmed. Repository risks such as secrets and dependencies and the deferred-L2 dimensions remain repo-wide, while path-convention candidates are annotation-only and platform suffix evidence is separate. The partition discloses that enumeration and reads come from a mutable worktree and makes no atomic snapshot or git-blob identity claim. Runs all 20 scanners synchronously (secrets, SAST, dependency/license, the platform quality-gate wrappers, the identity/PII/network regex battery, hidden-unicode, duplication, orphan-KB, a multi-language structural-metrics scanner, an opt-in foreign-Python type-check scanner that runs the target's own configured pyright/mypy, and a self-only rulebook-integrity check) with no inference — on a foreign target the platform-local scanners (code_quality/sql_access/orphan_kb/prior_pass/rulebook_sync) skip execution but stay in the coverage ledger as not_applicable so the roster never shrinks, and stack-gated scanners record not_applicable when their language stack is absent. The structural-metrics scanner (lizard, parse-only, every language) reports per-function complexity/length/parameter/nesting-depth distributions in a dedicated report section on EVERY run; it is report-not-gate, emitting band-crossing findings (complexity dimension, severity ceiling MEDIUM) only on foreign targets and suppressing those rows on a self-vet where the commit gates already own that surface. Two of the scanners are the TARGET's own toolchain — tsc (strict TypeScript typecheck) and eslint — which run ONLY on TS/JS targets AND only when the caller sets 'execute_target_toolchain' (default false), because they EXECUTE TARGET-CONTROLLED CODE (config JS, plugins, and node_modules/.bin binaries) on the scan host; prefer the Phase-2 sandbox, on-host execution is a discouraged flagged escape hatch — without the opt-in (or a materialized node_modules) they record a coverage gap rather than running. The same 'execute_target_toolchain' opt-in also gates the foreign-Python type-check scanner (pyright/mypy), which runs the target's OWN declared type-check configuration against its existing {.venv,venv} environment (the engine never installs or creates a venv); with no such config it records a distinct 'no static-typing contract' gap, and on a self-vet its finding rows are suppressed (the platform pyright --strict gate stays sole self authority). The self-only rulebook-integrity scanner (rulebook_sync) verifies the shipped assembled AI-critic rulebook still matches its committed hash manifest AND has not drifted behind its sources, emitting a HIGH code_quality 'stale_rulebook' finding plus a report integrity banner when the moat is stale or corrupt (self-policing so a stale moat never silently seeds the AI-critic pass). Optional 'scope' is a cosmetic label. Optional 'persist' (default false) writes this run to the vetting_runs trail as a side-effect so get_vetting_run can read it back by run_id (the joseki's payload-by-run_id seam) — the returned payload is byte-identical whether or not it persists, and a persisted L1-only run is recorded under substrate 'heuristic' (no inference), bounded by the same retention as the driver's trail. The minutes-long AI-critic (L2) and adversarial-verify (L3) stages are NOT part of this verb — they run as joseki-dispatched agent sessions.
embedding_description: Run the full deterministic security vetting suite over the whole codebase in one pass: leaked-secret detection, static application security analysis, vulnerable-dependency and license checks, operator-identity and PII batteries, hidden-unicode, code duplication, and orphaned knowledge-base detection. Returns findings ranked by severity and dimension plus a markdown report.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Object: run_id, target ({repo, ref, scope}; a foreign run also has source_role_partition and technology_fingerprint (scoped facts plus deterministic capability_needs; routing is not execution) — ref is empty in walk-enumeration mode), target_class ('self' or 'foreign'), enumeration ('git' or 'walk'), files_enumerated (int), stacks (detected language stacks — a subset of python/typescript/javascript — the engine's provenance for what the target is; gates the stack-specific scanners), started/finished ISO timestamps, total_findings, counts_by_severity (blocker/high/medium/low/advisory), counts_by_dimension, scanners_ran, scanners_total (the full roster; a foreign run's platform-local scanners are not_applicable, and stack-gated scanners are not_applicable when their language stack is absent — counted in the coverage but not run), coverage_gaps (scanners that could not run, with reason — 'not_applicable:' for platform-local or stack-absent scanners, distinct from a tool-missing gap; the target-toolchain scanners tsc/eslint and the foreign-Python type-check scanner record an opt-in gap unless 'execute_target_toolchain' is set and the target's env (node_modules / {.venv,venv}) is present, plus a distinct 'no static-typing contract' gap when a Python target declares no pyright/mypy config), and report (a bounded severity-ranked markdown register with a '## Structural Quality Metrics' section — multi-language complexity distributions + worst-offenders + a repeated-literal subsection (magic-string/value candidates, evidence-only) + a nested-loop subsection (loops within loops, a named static pattern class; ALWAYS rendered with its own examined-of-parsed denominator, including when the count is zero and when no functions were analyzable, because 'examined and none found' must not read the same as 'not examined' — the detector is Python-only, so absence in other languages is not evidence of absence; a foreign run also emits these as 'complexity:nested_loops' findings at LOW for depth 2 and MEDIUM for depth 3+) — and a '## Candidate Dead Symbols' section (unused functions/classes/methods/variables at 60% confidence from the in-process vulture scanner — evidence for the AI-critic layer, NOT findings; the provable dead-code classes unreachable-code and unused-import render as normal finding cards), truncation-marked if it exceeds the cap). The foreign source_role_partition carries the exact shared overall dimension histogram, unpartitioned repo-risk and deferred-L2 counts, only the surface-quality product/non_product/unconfirmed split, bounded overrides/candidate/platform evidence, exact reconciliation, and the mutable-worktree/no-blob-claim disclosure. The per-run structural-metrics distribution and the candidate-dead-symbols list are also persisted to the vetting_runs trend + L2-targeting trail.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Lead with the headline: total_findings and the severity histogram (blocker/high first). Name any coverage_gaps explicitly — a gap means a tool was absent or a scanner was not applicable, not that the code is clean. On a TS/JS target, tsc/eslint showing an opt-in gap is the DEFAULT (target-toolchain execution is off unless the caller opts in) — not a failure. Offer the markdown report for the finding detail. Note the run is a deterministic scan (minutes for the full toolchain), not an AI review; the AI-critic pass is a separate joseki. For a foreign run, present target.technology_fingerprint capability_needs as not-run routing needs, never as executed checks or best-practice verdicts; the scanner coverage ledger alone says which existing adapters ran.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Running the deterministic L1 code-vetting suite over the local git worktree.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: invalid_target_path: the supplied 'target_path' failed a fail-loud validation check — the message names which (not absolute / does not exist / not a directory / resolves inside or around the platform's own worktree, where self-vet is the default). invalid_role_overrides: the foreign-only source-role declaration list failed validation (wrong shape, more than 32, non-literal or unmatched prefix, duplicate prefix, invalid role, missing doctrine/declarer/session provenance, or any override supplied for self-vet). A RuntimeError about locating the worktree root means the verb could not find an ancestor of APP_HOME carrying both quality_gates/ and .git — the self-vet path is local-profile only and requires the git worktree (a cloud solet has none). A git failure from TargetTree means a git-mode target is not a readable git repo. An unexpected scanner exception is a real defect (the scanners convert expected tool-absence into coverage gaps, so a raised exception is not a normal condition).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: invalid_target_path: fix the named check — pass an absolute path to an existing external directory that is NOT inside our own worktree (omit target_path entirely to self-vet our own tree). invalid_role_overrides: omit the parameter entirely for self-vet or correct the named foreign-target declaration error; use normalized tree-relative literal path_prefix values that match the enumerated target and include doctrine_locator and declaring_session. Confirm the solet runs on a local profile whose APP_HOME sits under the git worktree for a self-vet (this plugin is excluded from cloud manifests by design). If a specific scanner raised, treat it as a bug in that scanner rather than retrying blindly.
